concept.name: Alligator indicator
concept.definition: Bill Williams' trend-detection overlay: three smoothed moving averages of the median price - Jaw (13-period, shifted 8 forward), Teeth (8, shifted 5), and Lips (5, shifted 3) - whose entanglement signals a sleeping (range) market and whose fanning signals a feeding (trend) phase.
concept.intuition: In Williams' metaphor, when the three balance lines intertwine the alligator sleeps and you do not trade; when they open and order by speed, it hunts and you follow the trend.
concept.mechanics: Compute the SMMA of (H+L)/2 over 13, 8, and 5 periods, displacing each line 8, 5, and 3 bars forward. Trend state: lines fanned and ordered (Lips above Teeth above Jaw for an uptrend); intertwined lines mean a range; lines joining after a trend mean the alligator is 'sated' - time to take profit.
concept.formula: Jaw = SMMA(MedianPrice, 13) shifted +8; Teeth = SMMA(MedianPrice, 8) shifted +5; Lips = SMMA(MedianPrice, 5) shifted +3; MedianPrice = (High + Low)/2.
concept.failure_modes: In choppy markets the lines braid continuously, generating repeated false wake-up signals - exactly the conditions Williams says to stand aside from, which the tool can only identify in hindsight.
concept.misconceptions: The forward shifts do not predict anything - they are display offsets of lagging averages - and the 13/8/5 'Fibonacci' settings are convention, not optimization.
concept.example: If the SMMA(13) of the median price is 100, it is drawn 8 bars ahead as the Jaw; when the Lips cross above the Teeth and then the Jaw and all three fan upward, the alligator is 'awake and eating'.
